newsitem.title: USA: US farm debt seen increasing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: US farm debt seen increasing in 1997.

text.p: Total farm business debt in the United States is expected to rise in 1997 for the fifth consecutive year to about $160 billion, Charles Dodson, agricultural economist for the U.S. Department of Agriculture said.
"Lenders and farmers, for the most part, enter 1997 in a financially strong position," he said at the USDA's annual outlook forum.

Dodson said much of an anticipated three to five percent increase in farm debt this year could be attributed to replacing aging capital stock. He noted problems were largely confined to cattle producing regions in the Plains and Southwest.
"Lenders and farmers affected by these events will continue to feel stress though overall conditions have improved.
Dodson said commercial banks had been increasing its share of farm debt in recent years at the expense of the Farm Credit System.
The FCS has in the past two years experienced an inflation adjusted increase in loan volume and was "well positioned to compete with banks for farmer's credit needs," he noted.
